m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The market's own price path aggregates news (injuries, lineups, sharp flow) and defines the executable price at each decision time.
m.quote_history.rationale: College basketball markets are far thinner and more numerous than NBA markets, so last-trade prints are often stale and midpoints with staleness flags are safer. The path also shows when lines react to lineup news, which in CBB is disclosed late and unevenly. Any feature must be joined point-in-time against the quote vintage, never against the close.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store every snapshot with exchange and retrieval timestamps; features: mid, spread, time since last trade, move since open, move in the final 2 hours; as-of join of model features (<= quote time).
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine how much can be filled at the quoted price and the round-trip cost.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: Mid-major and alternate-spread rungs are frequently wide and shallow, so apparent model edges there are often untradable; depth collapse before tip can precede lineup news. Edge needs to be measured net of half-spread and fees at realistic size.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Per rung: best bid/ask, size at best, cumulative size within 2c/5c, spread in cents and as fraction of price, hourly time-weighted averages before tip.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Traded volume and open interest proxy for how much informed participation has priced a market.
m.volume_oi.rationale: High-profile games (power-conference, ranked teams) attract more informed flow than low-major games, so identical model edges deserve different discounts. Futures volume is cumulative over months, so use deltas.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Cumulative and per-hour volume, open interest, trade-print count; rank of rung within event; ratio of volume to open interest; differences around news times.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: A strike ladder is a set of tail probabilities of one underlying quantity; internal consistency reveals mispriced rungs and the market's implied distribution.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Spread, total and player-prop ladders must be monotone, and the differences between adjacent rungs give the implied pmf; for CBB the residual sd (~10-11 points) and key-number structure are weaker than in football but ladders still expose stale or thin quotes. Rungs of the same game are heavily correlated, so edges across rungs are one exposure.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Extract all rungs for the same event/stat, enforce monotonicity, difference to the implied pmf, fit location and scale, flag rungs off curve by more than spread+fee, compute rung correlation for exposure netting.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The realized outcome and settlement time are the labels against which the whole system is scored.
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Needed for calibration but never a pregame feature. Subtle for CBB: box-score sources (ESPN, NCAA live stats) can be late or contain errors for smaller programs, so labels must come from the contract settlement and be reconciled with the named source.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Pull settled value, result and settlement time per market; reconcile with the source named in rules; flag disagreements and delayed settlements.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)
ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/mens-college-basketball)

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: Contract wording defines the event: whether overtime counts, how DNP or postponement resolves, push handling and the stat source.
m.rules_text.rationale: In CBB, period markets refer to halves (two 20-minute halves) and OT inclusion differs by market; player props may void or settle No if the player does not play; neutral-site, rescheduled and cancelled games (weather, travel) happen more often than in the NBA. The target must be matched to the wording per market.
m.rules_text.measurement: Snapshot rules text per market with hash; parse flags: ot_included, dnp_rule, postponement_rule, tie_rule, source_of_truth, strike inclusivity.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sportsbook prices are an independent, liquid estimate of the same distribution and embed injury and sharp-money information.
m.external_lines.rationale: For major CBB games sportsbook lines are an excellent prior; for small-conference games and player props they are sparser and later. The informative quantity is the de-vigged difference between Kalshi and the books, with staleness and who moved first.
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig lines, convert to implied mean/probability, track open-to-now movement and cross-book dispersion; Kalshi minus consensus per rung with staleness flag.
free_sources: The Odds API (free tier, limited credits; sportsbook lines)
ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/mens-college-basketball) (odds block, when present)

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.mechanism: Fees convert a probability edge into expected net return and vary with price.
m.fees.rationale: Fees peak near 50c, so the minimum edge depends on rung; long-dated futures also carry capital cost. The schedule changes and must be versioned.
m.fees.measurement: Versioned fee formula; net edge = model p - price - fee(price); breakeven edge by price bucket; capital cost for futures horizon.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule document (kalshi.com, free) and API fee fields

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Open, close, halt and postponement events define when information can be traded on and when a market is void.
m.lifecycle.rationale: CBB schedules change frequently (postponements, neutral-site moves, tournament brackets), and a market may close before lineup information is public. The true last tradable time per market is needed for point-in-time discipline.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Record open/close/expiration times and status transitions; flag postponed/rescheduled/cancelled events; minutes between last public availability news and close.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Realized hit rates by rung and price bucket reveal systematic miscalibration independent of any fundamentals model.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: With thousands of CBB markets per week the aggregate hit-rate table can be estimated precisely, but rungs within a game are correlated so effective sample size is the number of games. Condition on price bucket and line vintage.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settlements: realized frequency vs mean price by price bucket, by strike distance from the book mean, family and season; bootstrap by game.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: The tape shows realized execution prices, aggressor side and size, which give slippage estimates and informed-flow signals.
m.trade_tape.rationale: In thin CBB markets a single print may be retail; signed volume imbalances and repeated sweeps are more informative than one print. The tape also sets realistic fill assumptions.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Per trade: price, size, taker side, timestamp; signed volume imbalance in trailing windows, VWAP vs mid, price impact, time to next print.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

cbb.market_calibration_bias.label: Price-bucket miscalibration and popularity bias in CBB families
cbb.market_calibration_bias.mechanism: Retail flow and favorite-longshot patterns can leave systematic reliability gaps by price level, side and team brand.
cbb.market_calibration_bias.rationale: A reliability curve per family tells how far to shade model probabilities; brand-name teams (blue bloods) plausibly attract disproportionate over/yes money, but this is a hypothesis to test by comparing realized vs de-vigged-book expectation by team popularity. Subtle: separate calibration at rung level from game-level correlation.
cbb.market_calibration_bias.measurement: Reliability curves (realized vs implied, 5c buckets) per family x side, using de-vigged book lines as reference; interact with team popularity (national TV, historical fan base) and conference tier; game-clustered intervals.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

cbb.box_score_source_risk.label: Stat-provider reliability and settlement lag for CBB box scores
cbb.box_score_source_risk.mechanism: College box-score providers differ in speed and error rate, and corrections or incomplete stat entry can change a settled player stat.
cbb.box_score_source_risk.rationale: Smaller venues can have missing or delayed stat feeds, scorer errors on assists/rebounds, and ambiguous player-name matching, which makes thin player-prop rungs riskier. Knowable pregame only as a base rate by venue/conference and as the rules-named source.
cbb.box_score_source_risk.measurement: Compare ESPN, NCAA and Sports-Reference box scores for the same games to estimate disagreement rates by conference and stat; read rules_text for source and timing.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/mens-college-basketball)

cbb.implied_team_totals.label: Market-implied team points from spread and total
cbb.implied_team_totals.mechanism: Spread and total jointly imply each team's expected points and thus possessions and efficiency for every player in the game.
cbb.implied_team_totals.rationale: Implied team total = (total +/- spread)/2; it moves with news before box-score features update, and summarizes the book's view of pace and scoring for this matchup.
cbb.implied_team_totals.measurement: implied_home = (T - S)/2, implied_away = (T + S)/2 with S home spread; deviation from each team's rating-implied points; move since open.
free_sources: The Odds API (free tier, limited credits; sportsbook lines)

cbb.adj_off.label: Adjusted offensive efficiency (opponent/venue-adjusted)
cbb.adj_off.mechanism: Points per 100 possessions adjusted for opponent defense and venue is the core estimate of a team's scoring ability.
cbb.adj_off.rationale: Raw efficiency is distorted by schedule: a team playing weak opponents inflates numbers. Opponent adjustment via iterative/ridge methods is standard, but early-season ratings carry high uncertainty because few games connect the 360+ teams. Subtle: rating should be shrunk toward a preseason prior and weighted by recency and by minutes of the current roster.
cbb.adj_off.measurement: Ridge or iterative adjustment of per-game offensive efficiency on opponent, home/away/neutral and a recency decay; garbage-time filtering when play-by-play is available; shrink to preseason prior with weight rising with games played.

cbb.adj_def.label: Adjusted defensive efficiency
cbb.adj_def.mechanism: Points allowed per 100 possessions adjusted for opponent offense and venue estimates defensive suppression.
cbb.adj_def.rationale: Defensive efficiency is noisier than offense over short windows because opponent 3P% on open looks is mostly luck; it should be partially shrunk toward shot-quality-based expectation. Rim protection and perimeter defense differ in persistence.
cbb.adj_def.measurement: Same adjustment as offense; blend observed with expected defense from opponent shot quality; shrink early-season values; include recency and availability adjustments.

cbb.ratings.label: Power ratings (Torvik/KenPom-style) + market-implied
cbb.ratings.mechanism: A single opponent-adjusted team rating, optionally blended with market-implied strength, summarizes team quality for any game and for season simulation.
cbb.ratings.rationale: Free ratings (Barttorvik, Massey, Haslametrics, ESPN BPI) share structure but differ in recency, margin caps and garbage handling; averaging reduces idiosyncratic error. Market-implied ratings back out the teams' strengths from closing lines and often dominate in-sample rating-only models. Subtle: KenPom is paid and not a free source; use Barttorvik as the free analog.
cbb.ratings.measurement: Ensemble of free ratings (z-scored) plus ratings inferred from de-vigged closing lines (Bradley-Terry style fit on spreads); output mean and standard error per team; separate preseason, current and availability-adjusted versions.

cbb.preseason_prior.label: Preseason prior (returning production, recruiting, portal, coach)
cbb.preseason_prior.mechanism: Preseason expectations from returning minutes/production, incoming transfers, recruits and coaching continuity anchor ratings when current-season data is thin.
cbb.preseason_prior.rationale: The transfer portal makes roster turnover large and volatile, so last year's rating is a weak prior without a roster-based adjustment. The prior's weight should decay with games played and matter most in November and for early-season futures. Subtle: transfers' prior-team production must be re-scaled to the new team's role and level.
cbb.preseason_prior.measurement: Prior = regression on last-year rating, returning minutes share, transfer production (scaled by level), recruiting rank, coach tenure; shrinkage weight = prior_games/(prior_games + games_played).

cbb.rating_uncertainty.label: Rating uncertainty and schedule connectivity
cbb.rating_uncertainty.mechanism: The standard error of a team's rating depends on games played, opponent connectivity and roster stability, and determines how far to trust the number.
cbb.rating_uncertainty.rationale: Early-season ratings for teams that have played few, weak or non-connecting opponents have large errors, and a market line is more informative than the model there. Ignoring uncertainty overstates edges and makes extreme ratings look credible. Subtle: conference-heavy schedules limit cross-conference links, so conference-level strength estimates are themselves uncertain.
cbb.rating_uncertainty.measurement: Bayesian or bootstrap ratings producing posterior sd per team; features: games played, effective opponent link count, sd, roster-change magnitude; downweight model edge by posterior sd.
free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely)

cbb.in_season_improvement.label: In-season improvement trajectory (young rosters, rotation settling)
cbb.in_season_improvement.mechanism: Teams with many freshmen/transfers and changing lineups improve (or degrade) during the season, so average-to-date understates current strength.
cbb.in_season_improvement.rationale: Seasonal ratings treat all games equally; weighting recent performance and lineup continuity helps for young teams. Subtle: recency weighting overreacts to small samples and schedule noise; the effect is stronger in conference play and for postseason futures.
cbb.in_season_improvement.measurement: Rolling ratings with exponentially decayed weights per team; trend estimate (slope of residual vs line over last 8-10 games); interaction with experience/minutes continuity and lineup stability.

cbb.lineup_adj_rating.label: Availability-adjusted team rating for tonight's active set
cbb.lineup_adj_rating.mechanism: Team strength given who is actually available changes spreads, totals and every prop in the game.
cbb.lineup_adj_rating.rationale: A star guard missing in a game can swing a team several points, and with thin benches in CBB the swing is large; the market reprices quickly, so an independent player-impact estimate is needed to avoid simply copying the price. Subtle: pregame availability in CBB is poorly disclosed, so the model must carry a probability mixture.
cbb.lineup_adj_rating.measurement: Team rating = baseline - sum over absent players of (impact per minute x expected minutes), where impact from BPM/player-rating with shrinkage; scenario mixture with availability probability.

cbb.player_impact.label: Player impact value (BPM/EvanMiya/RAPM-style) with shrinkage
cbb.player_impact.mechanism: A regularized player impact value converts absences and role changes into team rating changes and anchors player-level projections.
cbb.player_impact.rationale: Box-score-based impact (BPM) and adjusted plus-minus approaches estimate value; CBB lineups have small samples, so shrinkage to a box-score prior is essential. Level of competition and role change after transfer matter.
cbb.player_impact.measurement: Blend BPM/box-score prior with regularized on/off estimates; shrink by minutes; adjust for competition level and role.

cbb.four_factors.label: Four factors (eFG, TO, ORB, FT rate)
cbb.four_factors.mechanism: Shooting, turnovers, offensive rebounding and free-throw rate decompose efficiency into the channels that drive both ratings and matchup interactions.
cbb.four_factors.rationale: Four factors reveal how a team wins (e.g. turnover forcing vs shot making), and their persistence differs: turnover and rebound rates are more stable than opponent shooting. Matchup interaction (one team's offensive rebounding vs the other's defensive rebounding) is more informative than aggregate rating alone.
cbb.four_factors.measurement: Offense and defense four factors adjusted for opponent and venue; stability-weighted blend (shrink eFG defense heavily); matchup interactions computed as team A offense vs team B defense relative to league.

cbb.shot_zones.label: Shot quality and rim/mid/3 mix
cbb.shot_zones.mechanism: The mix of rim, mid-range and three-point attempts and defense allowed by zone determine expected efficiency and variance.
cbb.shot_zones.rationale: Three-point-heavy teams have greater game-to-game variance; rim-heavy teams benefit from FT draws. Public shot-location data for CBB is limited, so it is derived from play-by-play shot locations where available. Subtle: coverage differs by conference and venue.
cbb.shot_zones.measurement: From ESPN/NCAA play-by-play shot coordinates (where available), frequency and FG% by zone for offense and defense; shrink FG% by zone; compute expected points per attempt and variance.

cbb.tempo.label: Adjusted tempo / possessions
cbb.tempo.mechanism: Possessions per game scale totals, team totals and every counting stat; tempo is a negotiated outcome between two teams.
cbb.tempo.rationale: Adjusted tempo is a stable team characteristic, but the game's pace is not simply the average; the team that benefits from a slow pace (usually the underdog) often exerts more control, and the late-game clock/foul behavior alters realized possessions. Subtle: possessions in CBB have a 30-second shot clock and halves of 20 minutes, so pace varies sharply by style.
cbb.tempo.measurement: Adjusted possessions per 40 minutes via opponent-adjusted regression; expected game pace = league + (A - league) + (B - league) with a tempo-control adjustment for the team that wants to slow; filter garbage time.

cbb.pace_mismatch.label: Tempo mismatch and who controls pace (possession-count variance)
cbb.pace_mismatch.mechanism: Fewer possessions raise outcome variance and help underdogs; the team preferring slower play often imposes pace, altering both totals and the cover probability.
cbb.pace_mismatch.rationale: Underdogs have greater win probability in lower-possession games because per-possession edges accumulate less; coaches also use tempo as a strategy. Expected possessions are therefore not just a total input but a spread-variance input. Subtle: the relationship is modest and confounded with team quality and shot variance.
cbb.pace_mismatch.measurement: Estimate residual sd of margin as function of expected possessions and rating gap; define tempo-control index (variance in pace across opponents); test cover probability for underdogs by expected possessions bucket.

cbb.defense_style.label: Defensive style (press, zone, pack-line, man) and turnover pressure
cbb.defense_style.mechanism: Defensive scheme changes opponent shot mix, turnover rate, free-throw rate and pace, creating matchup effects not captured by aggregate ratings.
cbb.defense_style.rationale: Pressing and zone teams create turnovers and variance; pack-line defenses limit rim attempts but concede threes; zone-heavy defenses allow offensive rebounds. Opponents' ball-handling quality and shooting profile determine whether the style is effective. Subtle: scheme usage varies by game state and opponent, so season averages blur it.
cbb.defense_style.measurement: Share of possessions in zone/press from tracking-like tags where available (else proxy via opponent turnover %, 3PA allowed rate, steals); matchup term = opponent turnover rate under pressure vs opponent baseline.

cbb.size_rebounding.label: Size, rebounding and rim-protection matchup
cbb.size_rebounding.mechanism: Height, offensive/defensive rebounding rates and rim protection determine second-chance points, interior scoring and block counts.
cbb.size_rebounding.rationale: Teams with large rebounding or size edges produce extra possessions; mismatch matters more than the aggregate rating, and affects player rebound and block props. Height data is imperfect for public sources. Subtle: lineup size varies by minutes.

cbb.repeat_matchup.label: Repeat matchups, scouting and conference familiarity
cbb.repeat_matchup.mechanism: In conference play teams meet twice (and again in tournaments); familiarity and strategic adjustments may alter the second meeting relative to rating expectation.
cbb.repeat_matchup.rationale: Second meetings can have a regression to the opponent-adjusted rating after an outlier first result and strategy adjustments, but evidence of systematic effects is a hypothesis to test. It matters for conference tournament games and bubble motivation.

cbb.home_court_team.label: Team-specific home advantage (student section, arena size, attendance)

cbb.neutral_site.label: Neutral/tournament-site effects and travel distance
cbb.neutral_site.mechanism: Neutral sites remove most home advantage but proximity (semi-home), travel distance and venue familiarity still shift performance.

cbb.opp_stat_allowed.rationale: Opponent-allowed stats by role are noisy and strongly affected by schedule; they matter mainly when defensive style is extreme (zone, press, big rim protector). Subtle: needs opponent adjustment (allowed relative to what opposing players usually produce) and heavy shrinkage.
cbb.opp_stat_allowed.measurement: Ratio of stat allowed to role-group relative to opposing players' season norms (ratio-of-ratios), shrunk by sample size; defensive style indicators; recency decay.
free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely)
Sports-Reference CBB (sports-reference.com/cbb; free, strict rate limit)
stats.ncaa.org (free official box scores and team stats)

cbb.stat_dist.label: Per-stat count distributions for CBB player props
cbb.stat_dist.mechanism: Player stat counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because minutes, role and game state vary, and the distribution shape determines tail probabilities.
cbb.stat_dist.rationale: Over/under at a threshold needs the full distribution: minutes scenarios and attempt dispersion; with fewer games per player than the NBA, parameter uncertainty is large and requires hierarchical modeling. Subtle: fitting only a mean plus normal sd mis-prices rung tails.
cbb.stat_dist.measurement: Negative-binomial/mixture models per player-stat with role-level priors; check dispersion and rung calibration; incorporate parameter uncertainty by partial pooling.
free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely)
Sports-Reference CBB (sports-reference.com/cbb; free, strict rate limit)
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free ESPN men's college basketball box scores and play-by-play)

cbb.recruit_exp.label: Experience, recruiting and returning minutes
cbb.recruit_exp.mechanism: Class composition and experience shape consistency, turnover rates and late-season improvement.
cbb.recruit_exp.rationale: Experienced rosters are steadier and often better in tournament-style single games; freshman-heavy teams have higher variance and larger improvement trajectories. Subtle: experience is correlated with rating, so partial effects are small.
cbb.recruit_exp.measurement: Minutes-weighted class/experience, returning minutes share, recruit ratings of rotation players, experience interaction with rating uncertainty.
free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely)

cbb.news.label: Coaching, award, ranking-poll news
cbb.news.mechanism: Coaching changes, player eligibility/transfer news, polls and award announcements change team strength and settle off-court markets.
cbb.news.rationale: Polls and award announcements follow rule-based timing and voter behavior; coaching moves alter roster and expectations; news flow drives markets in rankings and awards. Subtle: timestamps and source reliability matter.
cbb.news.measurement: Time-stamped feed from ESPN, NCAA, AP poll releases; derived features: ranking changes, coach changes, eligibility rulings.

cbb.bracket_sim.label: Tournament/bracket/seed/conference simulation
cbb.bracket_sim.mechanism: A simulation of conference play, conference tournaments and the NCAA bracket using team ratings with uncertainty yields probabilities for titles, seeds, advancement and conference outcomes.
cbb.bracket_sim.rationale: Single-elimination brackets compound game-level uncertainty, so title and advancement odds are very sensitive to rating differences and to the bracket path; conference title markets depend on remaining schedule, tiebreakers and the tournament format. Subtle: ratings must include uncertainty and injury scenarios, and bracket structure (regions, pods, seeding rules) must be modeled correctly after Selection Sunday.
cbb.bracket_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo: sample team strengths from posterior, simulate remaining regular season with home advantage, conference tiebreakers, conference tournament brackets and the 68-team NCAA field; model seed list construction or use bracket consensus; output pmf for advancement and seeds.
free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely) projections and tournament odds

cbb.resume_metrics.label: Selection-committee resume metrics (NET, quadrant record, WAB, SOR)
cbb.resume_metrics.mechanism: The committee selects and seeds teams using NET and resume metrics (quadrant wins and losses, strength of record, wins above bubble), so these predict bids and seeds beyond raw team strength.
cbb.resume_metrics.rationale: A team's chances to make the field and its seed line depend on a resume built from quality wins and bad losses, not only on predictive ratings; the committee historically also uses predictive metrics. Subtle: quadrant definitions depend on opponent NET and location, so records change as opponents move; the committee's weighting is not fully explicit.
cbb.resume_metrics.measurement: NET rank, Quad 1-4 records, WAB (Barttorvik), SOS/SOR, last-10 record; project final values by simulating the remaining schedule; compare with consensus bracketology.
free_sources: NCAA NET rankings and team sheets (ncaa.com, free)

cbb.committee_seed_model.label: Committee seed-line model and bracketology consensus
cbb.committee_seed_model.mechanism: Seed lines are determined by committee ranking of the field; consensus bracketologists' projections and historical committee behavior predict final seeds.
cbb.committee_seed_model.rationale: Seed markets are discrete outcomes near boundaries; the final seed depends on late results, conference tournament outcomes and committee quirks (e.g. treatment of conference champions, bracket balance). Subtle: consensus projections move with results and mix signals, so a model of the committee's ranking from resume metrics and ratings helps.
cbb.committee_seed_model.measurement: Ordinal model of seed on resume metrics and ratings trained on past brackets; blend with Bracket Matrix consensus average seed and its dispersion; simulate remaining results.

cbb.conference_standings_sim.label: Conference standings, tiebreakers and conference-tournament seeding rules
cbb.conference_standings_sim.mechanism: Conference champion and tournament-seed outcomes depend on remaining games, head-to-head and tiebreaker rules and the conference's tournament format.
cbb.conference_standings_sim.rationale: Tiebreakers (head-to-head, record vs top teams, coin toss) differ by conference and can decide a title or a double bye; many conferences have odd scheduling that leaves unbalanced remaining games. Subtle: details of each conference's rulebook must be encoded and updated yearly.
cbb.conference_standings_sim.measurement: Simulate remaining conference games from ratings with HCA; apply conference-specific tiebreaker algorithm; compute pmf of seed and title; include conference tournament bracket.

cbb.auto_bid_structure.label: Automatic-bid structure and one-bid conference dynamics
cbb.auto_bid_structure.mechanism: Many conferences send one team (the tournament winner); at-large bids depend on resume, so the conference tournament's winner distribution matters for a conference's bid count and for bubble teams.
cbb.auto_bid_structure.rationale: Auto-bid leagues have a high-variance single-elimination tournament determining the NCAA team; teams in one-bid leagues cannot rely on their regular-season rating. Bid-thief outcomes shift the bubble. Subtle: modeling requires the conference tournament bracket and bid-stealing probabilities.
cbb.auto_bid_structure.measurement: For each conference: tournament format and seeding; probability a non-top-seed wins; effect on at-large bubble by simulation of resume metrics.

cbb.conf_strength.label: Conference strength and cross-conference calibration
cbb.conf_strength.mechanism: Cross-conference games anchor ratings across conferences; conference-level strength shapes bids, seeds and the relative value of in-conference ratings.
cbb.conf_strength.rationale: Ratings within a conference are well-identified but conference-to-conference offsets rest on a limited set of non-conference games, so conference strength has uncertainty that propagates to futures. Subtle: the bubble is sensitive to this uncertainty.
cbb.conf_strength.measurement: Hierarchical rating model with conference random effect; offset uncertainty from non-conference game counts; compare to market-implied conference strength.

cbb.title_path.label: Bracket path, region strength and matchup-specific adjustments
cbb.title_path.mechanism: A team's title odds depend on its seed, region, likely opponents and style matchups along the path.
cbb.title_path.rationale: Equal-rated teams in different regions have different title odds; style mismatches (tempo, three-point reliance) matter in single games. Pregame information changes at Selection Sunday and with injuries before tipoff. Subtle: pre-bracket futures embed assumptions on seed/region that resolve at once.
cbb.title_path.measurement: After bracket release: path-specific game-by-game win probabilities from ratings and matchup adjustments; before bracket: expected seed distribution and region assignment uncertainty.

cbb.single_game_variance.label: Single-game upset variance by team style (tempo, 3PT reliance, depth)
cbb.single_game_variance.mechanism: Upset probability in a single-elimination game depends on both rating difference and variance drivers: low possessions, high three-point reliance and short rotations.
cbb.single_game_variance.rationale: Variance drivers modify the win probability for given mean margin; underdogs with slow tempo and high 3PA rate have inflated upset probability. Subtle: tests of this effect must separate it from rating differences and are noisy.
cbb.single_game_variance.measurement: Estimate game-margin sd per team-pair from possessions and 3PA rates; compute win probability from mean margin and sd; calibrate on past tournaments.
free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely)

cbb.seed_upset_priors.label: Historical seed-matchup upset base rates vs rating-implied
cbb.seed_upset_priors.mechanism: Historical advancement rates by seed and round provide a base-rate prior for tournament markets and calibrate rating-based models.
cbb.seed_upset_priors.rationale: Seed-based base rates give a long-run baseline, but ratings differ within a seed; the difference between rating-implied and seed-implied probability exposes market biases in futures (e.g. over-valued seeds). Subtle: sample sizes by pair are small and regimes change (expanded field, NIL/portal era).
cbb.seed_upset_priors.measurement: Advancement rates by seed and round over many tournaments (smoothed), compared with rating-implied probabilities; mixing weights fit by cross-validation.

cbb.star_injury_risk.label: Postseason availability risk for key players
cbb.star_injury_risk.mechanism: A key-player injury before or during the tournament changes team strength dramatically; futures prices must reflect the probability of such events.
cbb.star_injury_risk.rationale: A star's absence moves title odds sharply, and late-season injuries cluster; disclosure is limited, so pre-tournament availability is uncertain until the final days. Subtle: injury risk is rare but heavy-tailed, so mixture modeling is needed.
cbb.star_injury_risk.measurement: Hazard of missing postseason games from past data (age/minutes load/injury history), scenarios with impact values; update with news; weight by minutes concentration.

cbb.sos_remaining.label: Remaining schedule strength, location and rest
cbb.sos_remaining.mechanism: The strength and location of remaining opponents drive expected conference wins and seed outcomes.
cbb.sos_remaining.rationale: Unbalanced conference schedules leave equal-rated teams with different remaining paths; road-heavy stretches lower expectation. Subtle: strength must use current availability-adjusted ratings.
cbb.sos_remaining.measurement: Sum of per-game win probabilities from ratings with HCA for remaining games; difference vs league-average schedule; account for rest and travel.

cbb.popularity_bias.label: Team brand/popularity effect on Kalshi price vs fundamentals
cbb.popularity_bias.mechanism: Teams with large fan bases may attract disproportionate buying in futures and game markets, pushing prices away from model value.
cbb.popularity_bias.rationale: Blue-blood programs and ranked teams are plausible recipients of retail flow; the bias appears as a gap between Kalshi and de-vigged book prices correlated with team popularity. This is a hypothesis; the effect would be strongest in thin futures and alternate lines. Subtle: confounded with real quality and with line timing.
cbb.popularity_bias.measurement: Regress (Kalshi price - de-vigged book price) on team popularity proxies (historical title count, TV appearances, social following, rank) with game/team fixed effects; evaluate by price bucket.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (trade-api/v2: markets, orderbook, trades, candlesticks; free read, own-capture needed for history)

cbb.poll_voter_behavior.label: AP/coaches poll voter behaviour and rank-change dynamics
cbb.poll_voter_behavior.mechanism: Poll ranks move with results and narrative in patterned ways.
cbb.poll_voter_behavior.rationale: Markets on who is ranked #1 or how many teams hold the top spot depend on voters' reactions to losses and ranking inertia; strong teams losing to unranked opponents drop less than weak ones. Subtle: ties in the poll and week-of-season effects.
cbb.poll_voter_behavior.measurement: Historical week-over-week rank transitions conditional on result type, opponent rank and margin; fit an ordered-response model.
free_sources: AP poll archives (public)
Sports-reference CBB poll history

cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.label: Tier prior for unrated or newly reclassifying opponents
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.mechanism: Division III, NAIA and first-year D1 transition schools have no or almost no D1 games, so adjusted-efficiency ratings do not exist or are one-game noise; margin must come from a tier prior with a very wide sd.
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.rationale: The ledger lists a D3 game series and a spread strike of 50.5 against a D1 newcomer. A rating pipeline that silently fills these with the league mean gives wrong means and understated variance; the market in these games is thin and can be stale.
cbb.unrated_opponent_prior.measurement: For each opponent with fewer than 8 D1 games in the current season, replace its rating with prior = tier_mean + 0.5*(conference_or_division_mean - tier_mean) learned from past seasons of the same tier (D3 vs D1 buy games, reclassifying schools in years 1 to 4), in points per 100 possessions; set prior sd to the empirical sd of that tier's rating residual (about 3 times the sd of an established D1 team). As-of: use the rating snapshot taken before tip; update with the opponent's own prior-game results with weight n/(n+8).
free_sources: Sports-Reference CBB schedule and game logs
NCAA stats site D3 and D1 records
Bart Torvik (D1 only)

cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.label: Coach-specific bench-clearing and lead-protection behaviour
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.mechanism: How quickly a coach removes starters and what pace he plays once ahead by a lot determines how much of an in-game lead survives to the final margin.
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.rationale: Cover probability at large spreads is dominated by the end-of-game margin decay, not by the pregame mean. Some coaches play starters until a 30-point lead; others empty the bench at +20 by the second-half under-12 timeout. This is a stable trait across seasons (coach, not roster), unlike team scoring luck.
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: for every game in which a team led by at least 15 at any media timeout, compute lead_at_time_t (t = 12:00, 8:00, 4:00 remaining) and the final margin; coach_decay = mean(final_margin - lead_at_8min) per 8 minutes of game time, estimated over the coach's last 4 seasons with shrinkage weight n/(n+15) to the league mean decay, split by lead bucket (15 to 25, over 25). Also compute the share of second-half minutes played by the top-5 minutes players when ahead by 20 or more.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play (unofficial JSON)
Sports-Reference play-by-play pages (partial)
NCAA live stats archive

cbb.margin_regime_mixture.label: Competitive versus blowout regime mixture of the final margin
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.mechanism: Final margin is a mixture of a competitive regime (late fouling, overtime) and a blowout regime (compressed, coach-dependent), with the mixing weight a threshold function of the expected margin.
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.rationale: A single normal with sd 10 mis-prices tails at both ends: too fat in the blowout regime for favourites covering large numbers, and too thin right at tied-game and overtime-driven 1 to 5 point margins. Winning-margin buckets and 40+ point spreads sit in exactly these regimes.
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.measurement: Fit on historical closing-line-independent model expected margins m_hat: P(blowout)=logistic(a + b*|m_hat| + c*coach_decay) with a normal-in-regime margin for each regime (mu_k, sd_k) and a discrete overtime spike mass at margins 1 to 6 whose weight equals P(tie at 0:00) from the ot model; output the integer-margin pmf (for strikes at .5 and win-margin buckets) at pregame as-of; refit each season with at least 10 prior seasons.
free_sources: Sports-Reference and ESPN historical scores
own model expected margins

cbb.margin_total_covariance.label: Joint distribution of margin and total for same-game parlays
cbb.margin_total_covariance.mechanism: Margin and total are not independent: tempo and scoring-environment shocks move both teams' points together while blowouts reshape both margin and total through bench play and clock use.
cbb.margin_total_covariance.rationale: KXNCAAMBSGP is a conjunction of a spread cover and a total; pricing it as the product of two marginals mis-prices a systematic correlation, typically positive for favourites in fast games (favourite scores more, total higher) and negative when a slow favourite grinds.
cbb.margin_total_covariance.measurement: Estimate corr(margin_resid, total_resid) from standardized residuals (actual minus model expectation, divided by game-level sd) bucketed by favourite size (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+) and by team tempo tercile, with shrinkage to the pooled correlation weight n/(n+200) per bucket; as-of all prior games; apply through a bivariate normal copula with the regime mixture margins.
free_sources: Sports-Reference historical scores
Bart Torvik game files

cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.label: Point-in-time rating snapshots (no retroactive revision)
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.mechanism: Free rating sites recompute the whole season after each game and revise past ratings; a rating pulled today for a past date contains information from games after that date.
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.rationale: A backtest or live feature using the current rating page overstates edge via look-ahead; archival snapshots are rare and paid for KenPom. The strength gap input is only valid if it equals the number visible before tip.
cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.measurement: Store, each day by 06:00 ET, adj_off, adj_def, tempo, games_played, rank and the schedule-adjustment version for every D1 team from the chosen source; define the feature rating_gap(game) as the snapshot value from the last snapshot before tip minus the venue term; add snapshot_age_hours and an indicator for rating-method revision dates; for history use time-machine pages only where timestamps exist, otherwise rebuild from game results using a fixed algorithm.
free_sources: Bart Torvik time machine (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for full coverage)
own daily scrape from today

cbb.ratings_fundamentals.label: Fundamentals-only power rating ensemble (no betting lines)
cbb.ratings_fundamentals.mechanism: Team strength measured only from game outcomes, box-score efficiency and roster priors, so the opponent-adjusted efficiency gap carries no information that came from a sportsbook or Kalshi price.
cbb.ratings_fundamentals.rationale: The catalog input cbb.ratings blends free ratings with ratings inferred from de-vigged closing lines; using it as a driver makes the model partly a copy of the market and destroys the ability to measure edge against it. A fundamentals-only ensemble keeps the strength term clean; the market-implied rating is kept separately as a benchmark.
cbb.ratings_fundamentals.measurement: AdjEM_fund(team, t) = w1*AdjEM_Torvik(t) + w2*AdjEM_own(t) (+ w3*AdjEM_KenPom(t) only if licensed), points per 100 possessions, weights fit by minimising out-of-sample single-game margin MSE over prior seasons and constrained to sum to 1. AdjEM_own: ridge regression of per-game efficiency margin on opponent offence/defence effects plus a home-court term, exponential time decay (half-life 30 days), shrunk toward a preseason prior (returning-minutes-weighted prior-year rating) with prior weight worth about 8 games; uses only games finished before 00:00 ET on the tip date; no line, spread or price enters any term. Predicted margin = (AdjEM_A - AdjEM_B) * expected_possessions/100 + venue term.
free_sources: Bart Torvik T-Rank pages (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk history and as-of timestamps)
own computation from Sports-Reference / ESPN game results

cbb.possession_length_profile.label: Average possession length and transition share (offence and defence)
cbb.possession_length_profile.mechanism: Possessions in 40 minutes equal 2400 seconds divided by average possession length plus dead time; a team's offence length and its defence-forced length both matter.
cbb.possession_length_profile.rationale: A single adjusted tempo hides the matchup: a team that attacks early facing a defence that forces shot-clock-long possessions plays slower than the average of tempos suggests; this is the first-order total driver, since a three-possession error is about three to four points of total.
cbb.possession_length_profile.measurement: For team A vs B: APL_game = 0.5*(APL_off_A + APL_def_B) and 0.5*(APL_off_B + APL_def_A) in seconds from the season to date with half-life 6 weeks and shrinkage n/(n+10) to the league mean; expected possessions = 2400 / mean(APL_game) - dead_time adjustment (about 0.4 possessions per 5 team fouls above the mean); calibrate to realised possessions (FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TO) on prior-season games, output possessions and an sd. As-of: stats published before tip.
free_sources: Bart Torvik tempo tables
Sports-Reference team stats (possession estimates)
KenPom average possession length (paid)

cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.label: Overtime reach and repeat-tie chain
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.mechanism: P(OT) is the probability of a tie at the end of regulation (a function of expected margin, total and variance); each additional period needs another tie, with per-period tie probability set by five-minute scoring variance and fouling.
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.rationale: KXNCAAMBOT prices counts like 3+ periods, which need P(OT) times two repeat ties, a probability of order 0.1 percent that no ordinary total or margin model produces correctly. The same chain defines the right-tail mass of the points total.
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.measurement: P_tie_reg = integer pmf at margin 0 from the game's margin distribution (normal with sd = sqrt(poss/68)*10.5, centred at the model expected margin, with a discrete correction for the fact that tied scores cluster at lower margins); P_tie_OT = empirical rate of tied-after-OT among all OT periods over the last 10 seasons (per period, shrunk by count), with a multiplier for two-team free-throw rate; P(N+ periods) = P_tie_reg * P_tie_OT^(N-1); extra points per OT period = empirical mean (about 10 to 12 combined) with sd. As-of: pregame expected margin and total.
free_sources: Sports-Reference box scores with OT flag
ESPN scoreboard history

cbb.total_variance_by_style.label: Game-level total variance by tempo and shot mix
cbb.total_variance_by_style.mechanism: Residual sd of the total grows with the number of possessions and with each team's three-point attempt share, as scoring becomes more lumpy.
cbb.total_variance_by_style.rationale: Rungs near the mean are insensitive to the mean error but sensitive to sd; asymmetry in tails (fat-right from OT) means a single sd mis-prices both the over and the under side of high and low strikes.
cbb.total_variance_by_style.measurement: Fit log(var(total - expected_total)) = a + b*log(expected_poss) + c*(3PA_share_A + 3PA_share_B) + d*(FTr sum) on at least 5 seasons, with expected_total taken from the model not the market; output sd per game, and a skew parameter for the right tail (OT-conditioned). As-of: stats available pregame; refit annually.
free_sources: Bart Torvik game files
Sports-Reference box scores

cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.label: League-wide scoring baseline and rule-emphasis drift
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.mechanism: The national points-per-100 baseline changes by month (non-conference to conference play) and across seasons with rule emphasis, shot clock and officiating mandates.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.rationale: Adjusted ratings are relative to an average opponent; absolute totals depend on the current league mean, which moves several points per game between November and March and between rule years, and shifts early before ratings catch up.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.measurement: league_ppp_t = EWMA over the last 14 days of league-wide points per 100 possessions across all D1 games with half-life 21 days, plus an indicator for a rule-emphasis change flagged by NCAA rules committee announcements; expected total = sum of team unit ratings (relative) + 2 * league_ppp_t * expected_poss / 100; stored with timestamp so it uses only games completed before tip.
free_sources: Bart Torvik league averages
Sports-Reference league tables
NCAA rules committee announcements

cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.label: With and without primary ball handler: pace and efficiency shift
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.mechanism: A team's possessions per 40 and transition share change when its lead guard is off the floor, and its offensive efficiency changes more than defence.
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.rationale: Existing lineup inputs are labelled context and generic; the total contract needs the concrete delta in possessions and points per possession for the ball-handler absence scenario, weighted by the probability of that scenario.
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.measurement: For each team's top two ball handlers (highest assist-rate plus usage), estimate delta_poss = poss_per_40_off - poss_per_40_on and delta_ppp from on/off lineup splits over the last two seasons with ridge shrinkage lambda equal to 300 possessions off-court; scenario-weighted total shift = sum_k P(absent_k) * (delta_poss_k * ppp + poss * delta_ppp_k); as-of: lineup data through the previous game.
free_sources: Bart Torvik player on/off (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for lineup splits)
ESPN play-by-play for custom on/off

cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.label: Team pace elasticity to opponent tempo
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.mechanism: A team's realised possessions respond to opponent tempo with a team-specific slope: dictators hold their own pace, adapters match the opponent.
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.rationale: The shared possession count is where own-team scoring volume comes from. Using the average of two tempos assumes a common 0.5 weight, which is wrong for many pairs and shifts a team's expected total by 2 to 4 points.
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.measurement: For each team over the last two seasons regress game possessions on own adjusted tempo and opponent adjusted tempo (opponent-adjusted, centred on league mean): poss = a + b_own*(T_own - T_lg) + b_opp*(T_opp - T_lg); estimate b_own and b_opp per team with ridge shrinkage toward league coefficients (lambda equivalent to 12 games); expected game possessions for a matchup = league mean + b_own_A*(T_A - lg) + b_opp_A*(T_B - lg), averaged with the same computed from team B's coefficients, weights proportional to inverse variance. As-of: games completed before the prior day.
free_sources: Bart Torvik game-level possessions
Sports-Reference team game logs

cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.label: Coupling of one team's points to the game margin by role and spread bucket
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.mechanism: Given the total, a team's points equal (total plus margin)/2, so own points covary with margin; the covariance is not constant because blowouts reduce the total and cap the favourite's scoring.
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.rationale: A team total must be priced from the joint distribution of margin and total; treating team total as independent of the favourite or underdog role misstates skew and tails, and the coupling differs between favourites, underdogs and spread buckets.
cbb.team_points_margin_coupling.measurement: Estimate k = cov(points_A, margin_A)/var(margin_A) in standardized residual form by role (favourite, underdog) and expected-margin bucket (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+) using at least 8 seasons of games with expected margins formed as (AdjEM_fund_A - AdjEM_fund_B) * expected_possessions/100 + venue term, using cbb.ratings_fundamentals and cbb.venue (not market lines); shrink k toward the pooled bucket value with weight n/(n+250); simulate own points as 0.5*(T + M) with T and M from the regime mixture and covariance, then take quantiles at the strike.
free_sources: Sports-Reference historical scores
Bart Torvik

cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.label: Bench-unit and garbage-time-unit offensive efficiency
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.mechanism: Points per possession of units outside the top rotation (minutes below the top-6) is lower than the starters', and determines the favourite's scoring after starters sit.
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.rationale: In lopsided games the final 8 to 10 minutes are played by non-starters; team total at a high strike for a favourite depends on the efficiency of those units, which differs widely between deep programmes and thin ones.
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.measurement: From lineup data compute points per 100 possessions for lineups with at most 2 of the top-6 minutes players, over the last two seasons, shrunk to the team's starters-unit rating with weight n/(n+400 possessions) and to a league bench mean; stored with the share of team minutes played by such units when the team led by 15 or more (blowout minutes share). As-of: prior games.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play (derive lineups)
Bart Torvik player and lineup tables (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.label: Opponent foul propensity converted to the team's expected free-throw points
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.mechanism: The number of free throws the named team gets equals its drawing rate scaled by the opponent's fouls per possession and by bonus situations.
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.rationale: Free-throw points are a high-leverage part of a team total because they cost no clock; the opponent's foul rate is a stable team trait (pressure man defence or hand-checking) that the existing free-throw input measures only for the named team.
cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.measurement: expected_FTA_team = poss * [0.5*FTr_team_off + 0.5*FTr_opp_def_allowed] adjusted to league mean, where FTr = FTA per 100 possessions and both terms are opponent-adjusted over the last 20 games (half-life 8 games) with shrinkage n/(n+10); expected FT points = expected_FTA * shrunk FT% * 1; as-of: games completed before tip, crew effect added as +/- 0.6 FTA per crew standard deviation when assigned.
free_sources: Bart Torvik four-factor tables (FT rate offence and defence)
Sports-Reference team stats

cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.label: Team first-half possession share and early-game pace ratio
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.mechanism: A team's first-half possessions as a share of its regulation possessions differ from 0.5 because second halves have more fouls and stoppages, and the size of the gap is team and coach specific.
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.rationale: Scaling half possessions as half of the game's tempo mis-states the half total and half margin variance; teams that start slowly then accelerate are priced as if their pace were constant.
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.measurement: For each team compute r = (1H possessions)/(regulation possessions) per game from period box scores (possessions = FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TO per half), averaged with half-life 15 games and shrunk to the league mean r_lg (about 0.485) with weight n/(n+12); expected 1H possessions = r_team_pair * expected regulation possessions where r_team_pair = average of the two teams' shrunk r; as-of: games before tip.
free_sources: Sports-Reference box scores (period splits reconstructable)
ESPN play-by-play for period possession counts

cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.label: Coach policy: benching players with early fouls in the first half
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.mechanism: The loss of minutes from early fouls depends on whether the coach sits a starter after two fouls before the break and for how long.
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.rationale: Foul rates are stable, but minute loss is a coach decision: some coaches always sit at two fouls, others only after three or when the lead is large. Without this, 'foul trouble risk' is only half a mechanism.
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.measurement: From play-by-play, for each coach (last 3 seasons) take all starter instances with 2 fouls before the 8:00 mark of the first half; compute P(sit within 2 minutes of the 2nd foul) and the mean minutes missed until return, shrinking each to the league mean with weight n/(n+8); combine with the player's per-minute foul rate (opponent-adjusted) to give expected first-half minutes lost = sum over starters P(2 fouls by time t)*P(sit)*mean_minutes_missed. As-of: through prior game.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play (foul events and substitutions)
Sports-Reference play-by-play (partial)

cbb.half_tie_probability.label: Integer pmf and tie probability of the half margin
cbb.half_tie_probability.mechanism: The half margin is an integer with lumps of 1, 2 and 3 points, so its pmf has a central spike and parity structure that a normal density misses.
cbb.half_tie_probability.rationale: KXNCAAMB1H prices a tie as an outcome, and the 1H spread rungs near zero are also affected: each rung difference near 0 equals the pmf at one integer margin; mis-estimating the central mass by half a percentage point is a large error relative to the price.
cbb.half_tie_probability.measurement: Fit a discretized skew-normal or empirical-kernel model for the half margin with mean mu_h = 0.55*E[margin] and sd sigma_h = sqrt(poss_1H/34)*7.2, calibrated on at least 10 seasons of half margins; for tie, compute P(margin = 0) from the pmf with a correction factor c(|mu_h|) estimated from observed ties by expected-margin bucket (|mu| in 0-2, 2-5, 5-9, 9+); as-of: pregame mean and sd.
free_sources: Sports-Reference line scores
ESPN scoreboard history with half scores

cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.label: Halftime state update for second-half markets
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.mechanism: Conditional on the first-half score, foul counts and shooting luck, the second-half margin and total have means shifted away from the pregame values by a small fraction of the first-half residual.
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.rationale: The 2H series are live markets over the same game. The pregame prior plus an update on the halftime state is the correct information set, and the update is not 'trust the lead': most of a first-half lead is luck, but foul trouble and injuries are real.
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.measurement: Regress second-half margin on pregame expected margin, 1H margin residual (1H margin minus 0.55*pregame expected), starters in foul trouble indicator (2+ fouls for a top-5 player), team foul counts, 1H 3P% minus expected, and an injury-in-game flag, using at least 5 seasons of halftime states; output conditional mean and sd of 2H margin and total (including OT mixture). Typical expected coefficient on the 1H residual: 0.1 to 0.25. Not available pregame; knowable at halftime.
free_sources: ESPN live play-by-play
NCAA live stats feed

cbb.second_half_pregame_expectation.label: Pregame second-half expectation with late-foul and overtime terms
cbb.second_half_pregame_expectation.mechanism: A pregame 2H total or 2H margin is the full-game regulation expectation minus the first-half expectation, plus the second-half-only terms: intentional late-game fouling and overtime, which the 2H contracts include.
cbb.second_half_pregame_expectation.rationale: Three of the six live series (KXNCAAMB2H, 2HSPREAD, 2HTOTAL) settle on second-half points including overtime. The 2H distribution is not a mirror of the 1H one: it carries the full late-game foul script and the whole overtime tail, and the halves are not independent (coaching adjustments, garbage time).
cbb.second_half_pregame_expectation.measurement: E2H_total = E_reg_total - E1H_total + L + Q, where E_reg_total = expected regulation total from the game-total inputs (tempo, adj_off, adj_def; no market line), E1H_total from the first-half inputs, L = expected extra combined points from late-game fouling given the expected-margin bucket (|margin|<=6 at 4:00 left; estimated from play-by-play over at least 5 seasons), Q = P(tie at end of regulation) * E[overtime combined points per game that goes to overtime]. 2H margin mean = E_reg_margin - E1H_margin + OT margin term (zero mean). Variance: Var(2H) from empirical 2H line-score residuals by expected-margin bucket; estimate corr(1H residual, 2H residual) from 10 seasons of line scores without assuming its sign. As-of rule: all inputs known before tip.
free_sources: Sports-Reference and ESPN box scores with period line scores (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for complete period scores in all games)
ESPN play-by-play for foul and clock events (coverage uneven for small schools)

cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture by game state and foul risk
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: A player's minutes are a mixture of at least three regimes (competitive full minutes, blowout truncated, foul-trouble truncated) with weights set by the spread, the coach's rotation habits and the foul propensity.
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: A single expected-minutes number averages a bimodal variable; for a star on a 15-point favourite the 28-minute mode and the 34-minute mode generate very different probabilities of reaching 25 points, so the mixture matters more for high rungs than for the median.
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: Fit for each player-role bucket (starter guard, starter wing, starter big, rotation) a three-component model on minutes: component weights w_k = softmax(a_k + b_k*|expected margin| + c_k*foul_rate_per_40 + d_k*back-to-back flag), with component means estimated from last two seasons of games per coach with ridge shrinkage; output the pmf over minutes in 4-minute bins; as-of: spread-free (use model expected margin, not market line).
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs
Bart Torvik player game stats

cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.label: Location-based expected points per shot attempt with opponent adjustment
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.mechanism: A player's expected points per attempt equals the sum over shot locations of attempt share times league-average make rate times value, adjusted for the opponent's defence at each location.
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.rationale: Observed FG% is a noisy estimate; shot location (rim, short mid-range, long two, three, catch-and-shoot versus off-dribble) predicts future efficiency better than recent results, and regression should move the observed rate toward the location-implied rate rather than toward a flat league mean.
cbb.player_shot_mix_xpps.measurement: xPPS = sum_z share_z * (league_make_z shrunk with player make_z weight n_z/(n_z+60)) * value_z + FT component; opponent adjustment: multiply each zone's rate by (opponent allowed rate in zone / league rate)^0.5 estimated over the last 20 games with half-life 8; as-of: through prior game; units points per shot attempt.

cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.label: Player expected free-throw attempts: drawn-foul rate and late-game ball-handling share
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.mechanism: Player FTA equal drawn fouls per 100 possessions times possessions on court times a bonus factor, plus a late-game component for ball handlers on teams likely to lead or to be fouled at the end.
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.rationale: Free throws are a distinct scoring channel with its own distribution; late-game trips depend on the probability of a close game and on who handles the ball, so guards and wings differ even at equal usage.
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.measurement: xFTA = (drawn-foul FTA rate per 100 on-court possessions, last 20 games, half-life 10, shrunk n/(n+8) to role mean) * expected on-court possessions + P(close at 2:00 left) * (ball-handler share of late possessions) * expected late FTA per team (about 4 in a one-possession game); FT% enters separately with shrinkage n/(n+100) to 72 percent league mean; as-of: pregame.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player FTA and fouls drawn (derive)

cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.label: Player points dispersion index by role
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.mechanism: Variance of a player's single-game points relative to his mean varies by role (high-usage guard versus low-usage big) and by shot mix.
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.rationale: High rungs (25 plus) read the tail of the count distribution, and the tail width depends on role variance more than on the mean; using one dispersion for all players mis-prices the high and low rungs in opposite directions.
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.measurement: For each role bucket compute phi = var(points | minutes bucket, expected usage) / mean over the last 3 seasons of player games with weight to the player's own phi_i = n/(n+25) shrinkage; use negative binomial with mean mu and size r = mu/(phi-1) conditional on playing 15+ minutes, mixed with the DNP point mass; output per-rung probabilities; as-of: pregame.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs
Bart Torvik player game stats

cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.label: Early-game scoring profile and opening-possession edge for race-to-N markets
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.mechanism: A race to N points is a first-passage problem: the leader after the opening minutes is determined by the opening lineup's scoring rate, the tip or arrow possession and early turnovers.
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.rationale: The ledger classifies the only live series (Race to 10, 25, 50) in this archetype, but a first-passage event depends on points per possession in the first 8 to 12 minutes with starters, not on full-game efficiency; race to 50 additionally integrates to about the 28th to 30th minute and is affected by the substitution pattern.
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.measurement: From play-by-play compute per team the time series of cumulative points in the first 10, 25 and 50 point marks (minutes to reach each), as-of prior games with half-life 12 games; model lambda_A, lambda_B as points per possession of the starters' unit in the first 8 minutes (with shrinkage n/(n+10) to full-game ppp); P(A first to N) from a Skellam-type random walk in possessions with a first-possession edge of about 0.5 possession (tip or arrow, 50 percent) added; as-of: before tip, with lineup status.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play
NCAA live stats archive (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk)

cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.label: Cold-start role and rate prior for transfer and freshman players
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.mechanism: A player new to a team has no history in the current system; his minutes, usage and per-minute rates must be inferred from previous team production translated through quality and position gaps.
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.rationale: Because a large share of D1 rotation minutes (a figure to be measured, not assumed) is carried each year by transfers and freshmen new to their team, early-season props for newcomers are priced on prior-team averages even though role and competition change; the translation is non-trivial and is the largest source of early-season error.
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.measurement: For each newcomer with prior-season D1 stats: prior usage = prev_usage * (prev_team_ORtg_rank / new_team_ORtg_rank)^0.3 shrunk toward the new team's open-minutes distribution by weight depending on departures (minutes available = minutes of lost players / 200); per-minute rate prior = prev rate * conference-strength factor (from the KenPom/Torvik conference ratings gap; the per-tier discount, assumed between 3 and 8 percent, is to be calibrated) + position adjustment; replace with current-season rates as n/(n+10 games). For freshmen use recruiting rank (247 composite) mapped to expected BPM from history. As-of: portal status and roster at the decision time.
free_sources: Sports-Reference previous seasons
247Sports composite and portal tracker (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk export)
Bart Torvik player ratings

cbb.player_stat_covariance.label: Cross-stat covariance of points, rebounds, assists and threes within a player
cbb.player_stat_covariance.mechanism: Stats of the same player are positively correlated through minutes, pace and game state, with a residual correlation after conditioning that depends on role.
cbb.player_stat_covariance.rationale: Combination markets and parlays require the joint probability; independence overstates variance reduction and misprices points-plus-rebounds style thresholds in the tails.
cbb.player_stat_covariance.measurement: Estimate the 4x4 correlation of Pearson residuals of (points, rebounds, assists, threes) given expected minutes by role bucket using the last 3 seasons, shrink each correlation toward the role bucket pooled value with weight n/(n+40); simulate via a Gaussian copula with stat-specific NB marginals conditioned on a shared minutes draw from the minutes mixture; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs
Bart Torvik player game stats

cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.label: Role-stable effective sample size for shrinkage
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.mechanism: Games played in a different role (injury return, new starter, teammate absence) carry less information about today's rate than games in the same role.
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.rationale: Shrinkage constants set by raw game counts under-shrink players whose role changed and over-shrink stable ones; hierarchical estimates need the effective, not nominal, sample.
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.measurement: n_eff = sum over prior games g of w_g where w_g = exp(-age_g/12 games) * (1 if |minutes_g - expected minutes now| < 6 and starter flag matches else 0.4) * (1 if teammate availability set matches within one starter else 0.7); shrinkage factor k/(n_eff + k) with k = 12 games for rebounds, 20 for points, 30 for threes made; as-of: through prior game.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player logs
ESPN box score starter flags

cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.label: Home-venue scorekeeper bias in recorded assists, blocks and rebounds
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.mechanism: The official statistician's discretion on assists, steals and blocks varies by venue; the same player's recorded rate differs at home versus away after controlling for his true activity.
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.rationale: If a home venue systematically credits more assists, an over on assists is cheaper at home than the rate suggests; the effect is stable and cheap to estimate from the difference between home and away rates of visitors.
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.measurement: For each arena compute (assists per 100 team FGM recorded for the home team minus the same teams' away rate) minus league mean home gap, using 3 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+300 team games); likewise blocks per 100 opponent two-point attempts; apply as a multiplicative adjustment capped at +/-6 percent; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED that the effect exists in college data at this size.
free_sources: Sports-Reference team game logs home/away
Bart Torvik game files

cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.label: Cause-specific non-appearance probabilities (injury, coach decision, eligibility, suspension)
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.mechanism: Different causes of absence have different base rates, different warning signals and different timing, so a single status probability mixes unlike events.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.rationale: College players miss games for reasons that never appear in an injury list (coach's decision, academic or eligibility issues, return from injury minutes limits); treating all absences alike loses the signal that a long-listed injury is more informative than a quiet scratch.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.measurement: Classify historical non-appearances of rotation players (top-8 minutes) into causes using news and box score patterns; estimate P(appear) = 1 - sum_c P(cause_c | status label, days since status, program type) with Beta priors by cause (for example injury questionable: 0.55 play; undisclosed: 0.97 play) updated weekly; as-of: status vintage; output also restricted-minutes probability after return (minutes cap 20 in first game back).
free_sources: ESPN injuries and game recaps
team press releases

cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.label: Rebound competition from the other four players on the floor
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.mechanism: A player's rebounds are his share of a pool, and that share falls with the combined rebound rates of lineup partners on the floor.
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.rationale: Two good rebounders share one pool; when one is out, the other's rebounds rise by roughly the missing player's share. A per-player rate measured with a different lineup misstates tonight's rate; the effect is largest for bigs.
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.measurement: For each lineup scenario k (from availability probabilities), compute share_i,k = r_i / sum_j in lineup(r_j) * team_pool_share, where r is the player's rebound rate per 100 available rebounds estimated from the last 2 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+400 minutes) toward position mean; expected rebounds = sum_k P(k) * minutes_i,k/40 * pool_per_40 * share_i,k; separate for offensive (using team ORB%) and defensive boards; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik player ORB% and DRB%
Sports-Reference player advanced stats
ESPN play-by-play lineups

cbb.miss_location_mix.label: Expected location mix of missed shots (rim, mid-range, three) and perimeter rebound share
cbb.miss_location_mix.mechanism: Long misses from three-point shots produce longer rebounds that go to guards and wings more often, while rim misses go to bigs; a team's shot mix therefore reallocates the rebound pool among positions.
cbb.miss_location_mix.rationale: A guard's rebound line looks high in games where both teams shoot many threes and low against a rim-oriented opponent; position-blind pool totals miss this reallocation.
cbb.miss_location_mix.measurement: For game g, expected misses by zone M_z = sum over both teams of FGA_z * (1 - make_z) using team shot mix and opponent-adjusted zone make rates; perimeter share of rebounds by position from historical play-by-play: P(guard collects | three-point miss) and P(big collects | rim miss) with shrinkage; player-level adjustment: expected rebounds = sum_z M_z * share_player,z shrunk toward the position mean with n/(n+300). As-of: shot mix over the last 15 games.

cbb.assist_conversion_chain.label: Assist chain: potential assists times assisted share of teammates' shots
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.mechanism: Expected assists equal the player's share of team creation times the expected number of team assisted field goals, which depends on the mix of shot types (threes and dunks are mostly assisted, post-ups and isolations rarely).
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.rationale: The assist line moves with the team's expected assisted made baskets, a quantity forecastable from shot mix and shot-quality, not from the player's own assist average; scorer discretion adds a venue term.
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.measurement: expected team assisted FGM = sum_z FGA_z * make_z * assisted_share_z (opponent-adjusted, last 15 games with shrinkage n/(n+10)); player assists = creation_share_i (assists per team assisted FGM while on floor, last 2 seasons, shrunk to role mean with n/(n+600 minutes)) * team assisted FGM * (minutes_i/40) * on-floor adjustment for lineup partners; as-of: prior games and scenario weighting.
free_sources: Sports-Reference team and player assist stats
hoop-math assisted shares (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.label: Ball-handler succession: who inherits creation when the primary handler is out
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.mechanism: When a primary creator is absent, assists redistribute to the next handler in a team-specific order and a share of creation is lost because the replacement creates less efficiently.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.rationale: Teammate absence shifts are not symmetric across the roster; some teams have a clear second handler, others spread creation, which changes the sign of the replacement's assist line and the team's total assists.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.measurement: From with/without data over the last two seasons, for each team compute the change in assists per 40 for each rotation player when the primary handler (highest assist share) is off the floor, shrinking with n/(n+250 minutes) to a role-mean redistribution (such as 55 percent to the next guard, 25 percent to wings, 20 percent lost); output the redistribution vector; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play for custom with/without

cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.label: Shared game shooting shock with opposite loadings on rebounds and assists
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.mechanism: Game-level team shooting luck raises assists and lowers rebounds; the loading depends on role and is the source of the negative dependence between the two stats.
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.rationale: Combination props and parlays need this dependence; ignoring it overstates the variance of rebounds plus assists for guards and misprices both tails of a combined threshold.
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.measurement: Estimate a one-factor model on the residuals of rebounds and assists after conditioning on minutes and team pace, with the factor proxy being the standardised team eFG residual in the game; fit loadings lambda_reb and lambda_ast by role (guard, wing, big) over 3 seasons, with shrinkage n/(n+80) to the role pooled loading; simulate stats as NB with means shifted by lambda*z where z ~ N(0,1).
free_sources: Sports-Reference player and team game logs
